$comment: The Nano-only EXTENSION register (#1261, slice 6 of #1240). Nano is a strict superset of Camunda 8: anything Camunda supports must behave EXACTLY as Zeebe does, so the ONLY surface allowed to differ is what Camunda rejects or does not have — a Nano-only EXTENSION. This register is that surface's single source of truth. RULES (enforced by formal/parity/extensions.mjs, the CI guard): (1) every entry names an element/attribute/API Camunda REJECTS or LACKS, with a filed `issue`; (2) parity checks SKIP a model that uses a registered extension — an extension is out of the parity oracle's scope BY DEFINITION; (3) the register NEVER lists a Camunda-surface behavioural difference — a difference on Camunda's surface is a Nano DEFECT (tracked in formal/traces/allowlist.json or formal/corpus/divergences.json), never an extension; (4) a registered extension that Camunda is found to ACCEPT is not an extension and must be removed (the guard fails). This is the Nano-only counterpart of the coverage matrix's `out-of-scope` cells (formal/parity/coverage.json): those are Zeebe cells with no Nano meaning; these are Nano behaviours with no Zeebe meaning. Keep the two — and the allowlist — as THREE separate lists: out-of-scope = Zeebe surface Nano does not implement; extensions = Nano surface Zeebe does not have; allowlist = a DEFECT on the shared surface.

extensions.note: Per-element cost annotation (`<nano:cost value=… currency=… per=…/>` inside `<bpmn:extensionElements>`), read by processos' what-if annotation survey. Camunda 8 has no cost semantics; the tag is inert metadata to the engine (it deploys clean and never changes token flow), so it is a Nano-only extension, not a behavioural difference.
Per-element timing annotation (`<nano:time p50=… p99=…/>`), the duration counterpart of `nano:cost`. Inert to the engine; Camunda 8 lacks it.
Per-element role annotation (`<nano:role>…</nano:role>`), a processos what-if label. Inert to the engine; Camunda 8 lacks it.
Per-element service-level annotation (`<nano:sla>…</nano:sla>`). Inert to the engine; Camunda 8 lacks it. Stands in for the open-ended `nano:*` semantic-annotation family processos round-trips.
